p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (רמ״ו א), אִית לֶחֶם דְּאִיקְרֵי לֶחֶם עוֹנִי וְאִית לֶחֶם דְּאִיקְרֵי לֶחֶם פַּנַּג וְכוּלֵי.
— The holy Zohar on this portion (246a) teaches: there is bread called the bread of poverty, and bread called the bread of delight, and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ לֶחֶם עוֹנִי הוּא הַלֶּחֶם בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שְׁכִינְתָּא, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַסִּיהֲרָא דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ כְּלוּם,
— The bread of poverty is bread within the holiness of the Divine Presence, corresponding to the moon that possesses nothing of its own.
וְאָז צָרִיךְ צִמְצוּם,
— Then restraint is required,
וּכְמוֹ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁזָּכוּ לְלֶחֶם עוֹנִי וְנֶאֱסַר אָז הַשְּׂאוֹר וְחָמֵץ שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז לְיֵצֶר הָרָע.
— as at the Exodus, when they attained the bread of poverty and leaven and chametz, alluding to the evil inclination, were forbidden.
שֶׁאָז שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַיִּרְאָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ ה ב), דְּאִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בַּהּ יִרְאָה.
— For then fear is the root, as it says (Zohar I, 5b): she is fear, and fear dwells within her.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת זְמַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין חָמֵץ, שֶׁאָז זָכוּ לְלֶחֶם פַּנַּג, לֶחֶם ו׳.
— On Shavuot, however, the time of the giving of Torah, chametz is offered, for then they attained the bread of delight, the bread of vav.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז נִתְקַן הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה, שֶׁהוּא רַק מִמִּיעוּטוֹ שֶׁהוּא יָפֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לד.).
— The leaven in the dough is then rectified, present only in its small beneficial measure, as taught in the Gemara (Berakhot 34a).
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע יוֹעִיל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד.
— The evil inclination then serves to produce yearning for Torah, as will occur in the future.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ קלח א), אִלְמָלֵא יֵצֶר הָרָע חֶדְוָותָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא לָא לֶהֱוֵי.
— As taught in Midrash HaNeelam (Zohar I, 138a), without the evil inclination there would be no joy in Torah study.

h: Asher Transforms the Bread of Poverty

p: וְאָמַר, וְעַל דָּא מֵאָשֵׁר שְׁמֵינָה לַחְמוֹ, לֶחֶם ו׳ וְכוּלֵי,
— It says: therefore, “From Asher, his bread is rich”—the bread of vav, and so forth.
וַדַּאי הוּא יִתֵּן מַעֲדַנֵּי מֶלֶךְ וְכוּלֵי, דָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— Certainly “he shall provide royal delicacies,” and so forth—this is the Congregation of Israel,
דְּהָא מִינֵּיהּ אִתְּזָנַת, וְהוּא יָהִיב לָהּ עַל יְדָא דְּצַדִּיק וְכוּלֵי.
— for she is nourished from him, and he gives to her through the righteous one, and so forth.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ לְעֵיל (רמה סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳),
— This is as the holy Zohar says above (245b, end):
מֵעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי אִתְמְשִׁיךְ וְנָגִיד לְהַאי צַדִּיק,
— From the world to come there extends and flows to this righteous one,
לְמֵיהַב תַּפְנוּקִין וְעִדּוּנִין לְהַאי אֶרֶץ דְּאִיהוּ לֶחֶם עוֹנִי, וְאִתְעֲבִיד לֶחֶם פַּנַּג.
— to give pleasures and delights to this earth, which is the bread of poverty, so that it becomes the bread of delight.
וְזֶהוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ, שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק.
— This is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence, through the aspect of the righteous one.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלְּשֵׁבֶט זֶה נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן הָאֲכִילוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— This tribe was thus given the power to rectify acts of eating, making them holy.
וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ סא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), מְזוֹנָא עִלָּאָה יַתִּיר מִכֹּלָּא הוּא מְזוֹנָא דְּחַבְרַיָּיא,
— It is taught (Zohar II, 61b, end): the highest nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions,
אִינּוּן דְּמִשְׁתַּדְּלֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּאָכְלֵי מְזוֹנָא דְּרוּחָא וְנִשְׁמְתָא וְכוּלֵי,
— those who labor in Torah, who eat the nourishment of spirit and soul, and so forth.
וְאִיקְרֵי חָכְמָה וְכוּלֵי, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ.
— It is called wisdom, and so forth, as it is written, “Wisdom gives life to its possessor.”
וּמִסְּתָמָא אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת מְעוּלָּה עוֹד מִלֶּחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
— Presumably eating on Shabbat is higher still than bread from heaven,
וְהוּא כִּמְזוֹנָא דְּחַבְרַיָּיא דְּאִקְרֵי חָכְמָה.
— resembling the nourishment of the companions, which is called wisdom.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ, בְּסִפְרָא דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא וְכוּלֵי,
— Thus the holy Zohar says afterward: in the book of Rav Hamnuna, and so forth,
מֵאָשֵׁר שְׁמֵנָה לַחְמוֹ, דָּא לֶחֶם שַׁבָּת, דְּאִיהוּ פַּנַּג עַל חַד תְּרֵין וְכוּלֵי,
— “From Asher, his bread is rich”—this is Shabbat bread, whose delight is doubled, and so forth.
לֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה, תְּרֵי לֶחֶם, לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וְלֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ.
— Double bread: two kinds of bread, bread from heaven and bread from the earth.
דָּא הוּא לֶחֶם פַּנַּג וְדָא הוּא לֶחֶם דְּמִסְכֵּנָא,
— This is the bread of delight, and that is the bread of the poor.
וּבְשַׁבָּת אִתְכְּלִיל לֶחֶם תַּתָּאָה בְּלֶחֶם עִלָּאָה וְכוּלֵי.
— On Shabbat the lower bread is included in the higher bread, and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת הוּא הַיִּחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ,
— On Shabbat there is thus the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence.
וְהַסְּעוּדוֹת בְּרָזָא דְּעֹנֶג, עֵדֶן נָהָר גַּן,
— The meals embody the mystery of oneg, delight: Eden, river, and garden.
שֶׁהַנָּהָר יוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ כו סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳),
— The river flows from Eden to water the garden (as taught in Zohar I, 26a, end),
וְכוֹלֵל קְדוּשּׁוֹת כָּל שֵׁם הֲוָיָה.
— encompassing the holiness of the entire Name Havayah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 61b–62a; Zohar, Beshalach 28:377: “The highest nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions who occupy themselves with Torah. They eat the nourishment of spirit and soul, and do not eat bodily nourishment at all. It comes from the exalted place, more precious than all, called Chokhmah. Therefore the companions’ bodies are weaker than those of other people, for they do not eat bodily nourishment at all; they eat the nourishment of spirit and soul from a distant, exalted place, more precious than all. That nourishment is therefore subtler than subtle, beyond all others. Happy is their portion! Thus it is written, “Wisdom gives life to those who possess it.” Happy is the portion of a body that can be nourished by the soul’s nourishment.”

That nourishment is therefore subtler than subtle, beyond all others. Happy is their portion! Thus it is written, “Wisdom gives life to those who possess it.” Happy is the portion of a body that can be nourished by the soul’s nourishment.”

h: Asher Repairs the Root of Desire

p: וְאָמַר זֶה בְּשֵׁבֶט אָשֵׁר, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מֵהָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה,
— This is said concerning the tribe of Asher, in the manner of what I heard from the holy Rabbi, of righteous and holy memory.
שֶׁאָמַר דְּעָמוֹס שֶׁהָיָה מִשֵּׁבֶט אָשֵׁר, שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּקוֹעַ, אָמַר פָּרָשַׁת הֲלֹא כִבְנֵי כוּשִׁיִּים,
— He said that Amos, who was of the tribe of Asher and from Tekoa, spoke the passage “Are you not like the children of the Cushites?”
שֶׁהוּא מְיוּסָּד עַל צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי הַנְּעוּרִים, שֶׁהַפָּגוּם נִקְרָא מְכוֹעָר וְכוּשִׁי,
— It is founded upon the outcry of the young, for one blemished in this matter is called ugly and a Cushite,
שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁנִּקְרָא יְפֵה תוֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה.
— the opposite of Joseph’s aspect, who is called handsome in form and handsome in appearance.
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּשֵׁבֶט זֶה מָצוּי יוֹתֵר הַפְּגָם, עַד כָּאן דְּבָרָיו.
— This is because the blemish is more common in this tribe; thus far his words.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלְּשֵׁבֶט זֶה נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ בְּיוֹתֵר לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם וְקִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹרְשׁוֹ בַּאֲכִילָה.
— This tribe was especially given the power to rectify the serpent’s blemish and corruption, whose root was in eating.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִסְתָּעֵף שֶׁבָּא עַל חַוָּה וְהֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא,
— Subsequently this extended to his coupling with Eve and implanting impurity within her,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִסְתָּעֵף קִלְקוּל הַק״ל שָׁנָה.
— from which arose the corruption of the one hundred and thirty years.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁבְּשֵׁבֶט זֶה נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה,
— Since this tribe was given the greater power to rectify the root of the corruption in eating,
עַל כֵּן בּוֹ מָצוּי הַפְּגָם יוֹתֵר, שֶׁהוּא מְתַקְּנוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר.
— the blemish is therefore more common within it, for it rectifies it most greatly.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּשֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָה שֶׁבּוֹ נִזְכָּר הַפְּגָם בְּעֵר וְאוֹנָן,
— Similarly, in the tribe of Judah the blemish is mentioned regarding Er and Onan,
וּמִמֶּנּוּ יָצָא דָוִד שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים,
— yet from it came David, who is a root of life,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ רז ב), דָּוִד מַלְכָּא אִיהוּ חַי וְקוּרְבָא דִּילֵיהּ לְחֵי הָעוֹלָמִים וְכוּלֵי.
— as it says (Zohar I, 207b): King David is living, and his closeness is to the Life of the worlds, and so forth.
וּמִמֶּנּוּ יָצָא מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁהוּא גִימַטְרִיָּא נָחָשׁ,
— From him comes Mashiach, whose numerical value equals that of nachash, serpent,
שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן כָּל פְּגַם וְקִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ וִיבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח.
— who will rectify all the serpent’s blemish and corruption, and death will be swallowed up forever.
וְכֵן בַּשֵּׁבֶט הַזֶּה נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ בְּיוֹתֵר לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה וְכָאָמוּר.
— Likewise this tribe was especially given the power to rectify the root of the serpent’s corruption in eating, as explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 12:1: “The haftarah is ‘Are you not like the children of the Cushites to Me.’ I heard from our holy Rebbe that this passage speaks of the outcry of the young over the blemish of the covenant. The attribute of Yosef is called ‘handsome in form,’ a body clean and splendid; conversely, one who blemishes the holiness of the covenant is called a Cushite, as the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 36) says: Cham cohabited in the ark, therefore Cham emerged blackened. Yet of Israel it is written, ‘Do not look upon me that I am swarthy, for the sun has tanned me,’ for in truth all Israel are called righteous, as it says, ‘Your people are all righteous’; the darkness comes only from the leaven in the dough, and through the washing of teshuvah their beauty is revealed. Thus it says afterwards, ‘I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as one shakes with a sieve, yet not a pebble shall fall to the earth’: in the end all the souls of Israel will be clarified.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 1:1: “‘He made the letter tzadi rule over swallowing’: for the serpent’s first enticement was in eating, to make one feel the pleasure of the body, and from this the serpent came upon Chavah and cast impurity into her, and from this branched out the hundred and thirty years. Eating is the root of the blemish from the serpent, which caused the blemish of the covenant, and Asher brings holiness into eating so that it becomes words of Torah: ‘Come, eat of My bread.’”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 146a: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

p: וְאָמַר מֵאָשֵׁר שְׁמֵנָה לַחְמוֹ, דְּשֶׁמֶן מְרַמֵּז לְחָכְמָה,
— It says, “From Asher, his bread is rich,” for oil alludes to wisdom,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת פה:), תְּקוֹעָה מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁרְגִילִין בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת חָכְמָה מְצוּיָה בָּהֶם.
— as taught (Menachot 85b): because the people of Tekoa are accustomed to olive oil, wisdom is prevalent among them.
וְהַתִּיקּוּן לִפְגָם זֶה הוּא עִקָּרוֹ עַל יְדֵי חָכְמָה וְתוֹרָה,
— The rectification of this blemish is chiefly through wisdom and Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוּכָּה נב.), אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנוּוָּל זֶה מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
— as taught (Sukkah 52a): if this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the house of study.
וְהַיְינוּ לְהַמְשִׁיכוֹ לִקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִמֶּנּוּ חֶדְוָותָא דִּשְׁמַעְתָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד,
— That is, draw him into holiness, so that joy in Torah study comes from him, as will occur in the future.
וּלְתַכְלִית זֶה נִבְרָא,
— For this purpose he was created,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִידּוּשִׁין ל:), בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע וּבָרָאתִי לוֹ תּוֹרָה תַבְלִין.
— as taught (Kiddushin 30b): I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning.
וְהַיְינוּ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע.
— This means the evil inclination of desire, concerning which He says, “I created the evil inclination.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ דְּהַז׳ שֵׁמוֹת שֶׁל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁנֶּחְשְׁבוּ בְּסוּכָּה,
— As we explained, the seven names of the evil inclination enumerated in Sukkah
הֵם רוֹמְזִים בְּזֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה נֶגֶד הַז׳ מִדּוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— allude, on the opposing side, to counterparts of the seven holy attributes.
וְהַיֵּצֶר מִתַּאֲוָה הוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת הַחֶסֶד,
— The inclination toward desire corresponds to the attribute of Chesed.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קְרָאוֹ רַע,
— Of this it says, the Holy One, blessed be He, called it evil,
שֶׁהַפּוֹגֵם נִקְרָא רַע בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם, וְהוּא הַפְּסוֹלֶת מִבְּחִינַת הַחֶסֶד כַּיָּדוּעַ
— for one who causes this blemish is called evil in Hashem’s eyes; it is the dross of Chesed, as is known
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית).
— (and as explained at the end of Bereishit).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik §218: “The creation of the inclination in a person, however, is in the domain of desire, which also has a good aspect in ardent love of Torah. Of this the Sages said, ‘I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its seasoning.’ Torah seasons it and makes it food fit to be within the camp of Israel. … By using one’s strength and anger for good, one cannot conquer the trait of anger, for one may also come to evil anger. Rather, conquest here too comes through Torah: when one desires only Torah, one consequently does not desire worldly matters at all, and does not become angry over them or jealous of them, but only in matters of Torah.”

rich.text: Parallel:
Tzidkat HaTzadik §218

: “The creation of the inclination in a person, however, is in the domain of desire, which also has a good aspect in ardent love of Torah. Of this the Sages said, ‘I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its seasoning.’ Torah seasons it and makes it food fit to be within the camp of Israel. … By using one’s strength and anger for good, one cannot conquer the trait of anger, for one may also come to evil anger. Rather, conquest here too comes through Torah: when one desires only Torah, one consequently does not desire worldly matters at all, and does not become angry over them or jealous of them, but only in matters of Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: “Seasoning” changes the direction of desire itself, so its energy can become the joy of learning described here. Rav Tzadok also identifies a further consequence: when worldly objects lose their hold on desire, the anger and rivalry attached to them lose their ordinary fuel.

The Holy One, blessed be He, called it “evil,” as it is written, “For the inclination of a person’s heart is evil from his youth.” Moses called it “uncircumcised,” as it is written, “Circumcise the foreskin of your heart.” David called it “impure,” as it is written, “Create for me a pure heart, O God”—implying that there is an impure heart.”

p: וּכְתִיב אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר כְּבִרְכָתוֹ בֵּרַךְ אוֹתָם,
— It is written, “Each according to his blessing, he blessed them.”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּלַל לְכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּבִרְכַּת כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים,
— He included every tribe in the blessing of all the tribes,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא וְהוּבָא בְּרַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי).
— as taught in Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma and cited by Rashi.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ הַזֶּה לְתַקֵּן כָּל הָאֲכִילוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
— Thus all Israel were given this power to rectify all eating, making it holy,
וּלְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
— and to rectify the serpent’s blemish completely.
וּבְשַׁבָּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים,
— On Shabbat all Israel are like Torah scholars, as explained many times.
וְשַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— Shabbat belongs to the mystery of the covenant, as the holy Zohar teaches.
וְהוּא הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה לְהַכְנִיס תַּאֲוָה בַּאֲכִילָה,
— It is the time to rectify the serpent’s blemish of introducing desire into eating,
וְנִסְתָּעֵף מִמֶּנּוּ בְּכָל עִנְיְנֵי הַתַּאֲוָה.
— from which it extended into all matters of desire.
וְזוֹכִין בְּשַׁבָּת לְלֶחֶם פַּנַּג דְּאִתְכְּלִיל לֶחֶם תַּתָּאָה בְּלֶחֶם עִלָּאָה.
— On Shabbat one attains the bread of delight, with the lower bread included in the higher bread.

Therefore it says, “He blessed them.””

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 6:1: “The Shabbat meal is the rectification of the blemish of eating, for the Shabbat meal is called the King’s feast, which is like eating the offerings, in holiness; and like the eating of a Torah scholar, for one who feeds him is like one who offers the daily offerings, and one who gives him wine to drink is like one who pours libations on the altar. We have already said that Shabbat eating is the eating of a Torah scholar, as it says (Shabbat 119a): ‘Had we known you were coming…’ — he replied, ‘Is any of you more precious to us than she?’ That is, the additional soul, which is called Shabbat as the holy Zohar says, is with each one of Israel like hosting a Torah scholar in his home, and the Shabbat meal is like offering the daily offerings and pouring libations upon the altar; it is like the eating of offerings.”

rich.text: Parallel:
Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 6:1

: “The Shabbat meal is the rectification of the blemish of eating, for the Shabbat meal is called the King’s feast, which is like eating the offerings, in holiness; and like the eating of a Torah scholar, for one who feeds him is like one who offers the daily offerings, and one who gives him wine to drink is like one who pours libations on the altar. We have already said that Shabbat eating is the eating of a Torah scholar, as it says (Shabbat 119a): ‘Had we known you were coming…’ — he replied, ‘Is any of you more precious to us than she?’ That is, the additional soul, which is called Shabbat as the holy Zohar says, is with each one of Israel like hosting a Torah scholar in his home, and the Shabbat meal is like offering the daily offerings and pouring libations upon the altar; it is like the eating of offerings.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Miketz 6 explains the claim that on Shabbat all Israel are like Torah scholars: the additional soul makes every Jew’s home a host to a Torah scholar. His Shabbat meal therefore has the standing of feeding a scholar and of eating the offerings, which repairs the blemish of eating.
